# Review Home Base — First Principles Engine

> **What this is:** the single anchor for the Barnes homeschool app's architecture & functional review.
> **Where reviewing happens:** a dedicated Claude.ai chat (the "home base"). It owns the recurring
> audit, holds the live issue ledger, and spins out fix runs.
> **Where fixing happens:** Claude Code web, driven by the prompts in `prompts/`, reviewed before merge.
> **Repo:** github.com/barnes-ngb/first-principles-engine · **Live:** first-principles-engine.web.app
> **Created:** 2026-05-29 · **Last audit:** 2026-09-08 (`LEARNING_MODEL_CENSUS_2026-09.md` — AUDIT-217, a read-only census of the learner model: the two concept graphs, every writer of `conceptStates`, every capture surface measured against whether its content reaches the model, and what recall exists; 60 nodes / 80 edges / 5 bridges, and of nineteen capture surfaces only five carry their content into concept states, and the headline is that **nothing but a hidden `?diag=1` button can create the model at all** — UX-286 → UX-301; prior: 2026-09-05 `ASK_AI_AUDIT_2026-09_PART_A.md` — Ask AI functional audit part A, the eleven record-write action kinds + the chat's image door, FEAT-192a; also 2026-09-05, `AI_DEVELOPMENT_REVIEW_20260905.md` — external AI-development and documentation review, DOC-20, landed 2026-09-06 by DOC-21 with its unapplied corrections tracked there rather than assumed applied; prior area audits: `UX_AUDIT_BOOKS_2026-09.md` 2026-09-03, `STYLE_AUDIT_2026-09.md`; last full architecture audit: 2026-08-30 `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-30.md`; prior: August 23 mid-cycle audit `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-23.md`, August 16 mid-cycle audit `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-16.md`, August 9 mid-cycle re-verification `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-09.md`, August 2 primary monthly run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08.md`, July 26 run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-26.md`, July 19 primary run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-19.md`, July 12 mid-cycle re-verification `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-12.md`, July 5 run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07.md`, June 28 run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-06-28.md`, June 21 mid-cycle supplement, primary June run: `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-06.md`)

---

## 1. Why this exists

The project already has a working maintenance system (Tiers 1–3 below) that keeps stats and docs
honest every few days. What it lacked was **teeth on architecture** and a path from *finding* to *fix*.
This home base adds that: one recurring deep audit focused on structure and the end-to-end loop, plus
a repeatable fix runner so issues don't just get logged — they get closed.

## 2. Review priority order

Set by Nathan, 2026-05-29. The audit and ledger weight findings in this order:

1. **Architecture & tech debt** — structure, decomposition, bundle, test coverage. *(primary)*
2. **Functional / UX completeness** — does the evaluate → plan → execute → review loop actually work for Shelly and the boys.
3. **Pedagogy & ethos alignment** — charter fidelity, disposition-over-mastery, no-shame, coverage-not-pace.
4. **Data integrity & compliance** — hours aggregation, MO 600-core line, source-of-truth conflicts.

> Note: an item in a lower band still jumps the queue if it is **time-sensitive or compliance-critical**
> (e.g. DATA-01 below, which affects the June 30 MO core-hours line).

## 3. How to run the home base

| Action | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Monthly deep audit** | Claude Code web (scheduled) | Run `prompts/PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md`. Same scheduling mechanism as your /3-day health audit. Suggested: 1st of month, after the health audit. |
| **Fix an issue** | Claude Code web (manual) | Run `prompts/PROMPT_FIX.md` with one issue ID from the ledger (§6). |
| **Strategy / triage / "should we even do this"** | Claude.ai home-base chat | Paste this file + the latest dated audit report. Talk it through. Decisions land back in the ledger. |
| **Refresh project context** | Claude.ai project settings | Point the project at `docs/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (regenerated weekly by Tier 3), not the stale v14 outline. See DOC-01. |

## 4. The existing maintenance system (unchanged — for reference)

| Tier | Cadence | Output | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — Health Audit** | every 3 days | `docs/HEALTH_REPORT.md` (stats, build/lint/test, doc drift, auto-fixes numbers) | Claude Code scheduled |
| **2 — Fix Companion** | after Tier 1 | auto-fixes mechanical doc gaps (undocumented tasks, missing collections, nav, index) | Claude Code scheduled |
| **3 — Context Gather** | weekly | `docs/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (AI-optimized context for design chats) | Claude Code scheduled |
| **4 — Deep Audit** | **monthly (this system)** | dated `docs/review/ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_<YYYY-MM>.md` + ledger update | Home base → Claude Code |

Tiers 1–3 stay as they are. This home base **is** Tier 4, made concrete.

## 5. Architecture map (as of 2026-05-29)

**Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite · Firebase (Auth/Firestore/Storage/Functions/Hosting) · MUI ·
Three.js r128 (3D avatar) · Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 4.6 primary, Haiku 4.5 for routine chat) ·
OpenAI gpt-image-1.5 (image generation — migrated from DALL-E 3 + gpt-image-1 per PR #1217).

**Scale (verified against code 2026-06-20):** ~180,429 TS lines · 117 commits on main ·
37 Firestore collections · 25 Cloud Functions · 19 chat task types · 34 routes · 181 test files ·
2,746 tests passing · build/lint/tsc all green.

**The core loop (this is what "functional review" traces):**

```
Evaluate ──► Skill Snapshot ──► Plan My Week ──► Daily checklist (Today) ──► Weekly Review
   ▲              (priority skills,                  (evidence: completion,        │
   │               supports, stop rules,             engagement, mastery,         │
   └───────────────conceptual blocks)                minutes, artifacts) ─────────┘
```

**AI pipeline:** 17 task types dispatched via `functions/src/ai/tasks/` registry; per-task context
slices in `functions/src/ai/contextSlices.ts`; charter preamble injected into all calls.

**Feature homes:** `today/` · `planner-chat/` · `quest/` (Knowledge Mine) · `avatar/` (Hero Hub) ·
`books/` · `workshop/` · `shelly-chat/` (Ask AI) · `evaluate/` · `records/` · `dad-lab/` · `progress/`.

**The central architecture tension (already named in `first-principles-system-review.md`):**
the system can answer *"where is Lincoln right now?"* from **six** places — Skill Snapshot, Ladders,
Milestones, Learning Map, Curriculum position, Disposition profile — and **none is authoritative**.
The loop isn't missing; it has too many overlapping truths. Sharpening that authority is the single
highest-leverage architecture move. Tracked as **FUNC-01**.

## 6. Live issue ledger

Status: `OPEN` · `IN PROGRESS` · `FIXED` · `WONTFIX` · `NEEDS-DATA` (requires live Firestore export).
Band = priority band from §2. The audit prompt updates this table; the fix prompt flips status.

**Lanes (ID-prefix legend):** **Structure** — `ARCH` / `TEST` / `LINT` · **Functionality** — `FEAT` / `FUNC` · **Docs** — `DOC` / `ETHOS` · **Data/compliance** — `DATA`.

> **Before appending a row, re-fetch the ledger from `origin/main` and use `max(id)+1` per lane** — concurrent chats can't see each other's pending rows (see the ARCH-18 dup reconciled 2026-06-07, and the bulk dedup of 2026-06-08).

> **Only one ledger-touching run should be in flight at a time across all chats.** Merge it before dispatching the next — `max(id)+1` only protects *sequential* writes; parallel cross-chat appends still collide on the shared counter (the root cause of every duplicate ID swept so far).

> **The avatar / Hero Hub lane uses a distinct `AV-` ID prefix** (`AV-NN`) for its rows going forward, so its appends can't collide with home-base `ARCH-NN`. (Convention for future rows only — existing avatar rows keep their `ARCH-` IDs.)

> **London-specific work lives in `docs/LONDON_BACKLOG.md`, not as `FEAT-` rows.** Per the Lincoln-first /
> London-minimal policy (`CLAUDE.md` › AI Development Operating Model), London touchpoints are tracked
> surface-by-surface in that register to keep this active ledger Lincoln-focused.

Lives in `core` so it's outside the DOC-09 `src/features` scan. **(2)** planner path — `persistConversation`'s `getDoc` wrapped in `withTransientRetry`; a `TransientConnectivityError` is caught, logged at **warn**, and swallowed with an honest non-crashing notice ("You went offline — your draft is safe here and will sync when you reconnect"), while **genuine faults rethrow** (boundary behavior unchanged). **(3)** foreground retry — `ErrorBoundary` now classifies both entry points (`getDerivedStateFromError` + the `unhandledrejection` handler): a transient error shows a gentle **"Reconnecting…"** state (not the crash screen), and a `visibilitychange → visible` listener **auto-clears** it on return to the foreground (children re-render, the recovered draft is still in client state); genuine errors keep the full "Something went wrong" crash and do **not** auto-clear. **Recovery win:** returning to the tab clears the transient boundary and the completed draft is waiting (client state survives because the page no longer reloads; the last successfully-persisted draft also reloads from `plannerConversations`). **Class coverage:** the shared helper + the `ErrorBoundary` net protect every flow; only the planner call-site is wired this slice — **follow-ups** (belt-and-suspenders, all already try/catch-guarded today so none currently crash): route synthesis / weekly-review / monthly-review / photo-extraction reads through `withTransientRetry` for honest named exhaustion instead of silent snacks. **DOC-09:** the census is **unchanged** (8 remote-guard · 1 image-downscale · 93 silent catch(es)) — the helper is in `core` (unscanned), and the new planner `catch` rethrows genuine + logs warn, so it is not a silent catch. **Verify:** `tsc -b` clean; Fix: on exhaustion, instead of dropping, issue a `setDoc(ref, {...updates, updatedAt}, {merge:true})` — a WRITE enters the Firestore SDK's in-memory mutation queue (reads don't) and flushes on the next same-session reconnect, so the "will sync" notice now holds (surviving a hard reload/eviction before reconnect stays the deferred durable-draft work; the draft also lives in React state meanwhile). **(P2, ErrorBoundary)** the transient auto-clear relied *solely* on a future `visibilitychange`, so a blip recorded while the tab was already visible (or a queued rejection drained after the foreground transition) never cleared. | **FUNC-10** | 2 | **FIXED** | **Chapter-question generation no longer writes `chapterTitle: undefined` for untitled chapters (shared `buildChapterPoolItem`; fixes `setDoc` invalid-argument on Prince Caspian et al. across TodayPage/DevAdminTab/PlannerChatPage).** Generating chapter questions for any book added without per-chapter titles (e.g. Prince Caspian, 15 untitled chapters) failed on every entry point with `FirebaseError: [code=invalid-argument]: setDoc() called with invalid data. Unsupported field value: undefined`. **Root cause:** three duplicated create paths each mapped pool items with `chapterTitle: <chapter>?.title`, which is `undefined` for untitled chapters; the app's Firestore is plain `getFirestore(app)` (no `ignoreUndefinedProperties`), so a `chapterTitle: undefined` inside a `questionPool` item makes `setDoc` reject the whole `BookProgress` doc. `chapterTitle` was the only offender — the top-level `BookProgress` literals correctly omit their optionals. **Fix:** one shared `buildChapterPoolItem(q, chapterTitle?)` in `chapterPool.logic.ts` that **omits `chapterTitle` entirely** when there's no title (spreads `...(chapterTitle ? { chapterTitle } : {})`, never `undefined`) and returns `null` for malformed questions (missing/empty `questionType`/`question`) so callers `.filter(...)` them out. All three sites (`TodayPage.tsx`, `DevAdminTab.tsx`, `PlannerChatPage.tsx`) now map through it — same questions, same write, same `BookProgress` shape; titled books still carry titles onto pool items. Existing/already-answered pools untouched (create-mapping only). **Behavior-verified:** Prince Caspian (15 untitled chapters) → Generate chapter questions (Today + Settings dev) succeeds, pool fills 15/15, no Firestore error. No `ignoreUndefinedProperties` flip (deliberately out of scope — would mask real bugs app-wide). Branch `claude/pensive-dirac-4wj1yk`. | `src/features/today/chapterPool.logic.ts` (+`buildChapterPoolItem`/`RawChapterQuestion`, +4 tests in `chapterPool.logic.test.ts`), `src/features/today/TodayPage.tsx`, `src/features/settings/DevAdminTab.tsx`, `src/features/planner-chat/PlannerChatPage.tsx` |
| **FUNC-11** | 2 | **FIXED** | **`openChatWithContext` no longer writes `context.weekTheme`/`context.itemTitle: undefined` (omits absent fields); fixes the Today "Find a video" button crash (`addDoc` invalid-argument).** Tapping **Find a video** on a Today plan item threw `FirebaseError: [code=invalid-argument]: Function addDoc() called with invalid data. Unsupported field value: undefined (found in field context.weekTheme ...)`. **Root cause (same `undefined`-field class as FUNC-10, different write path):** `handleFindVideo` (`TodayChecklist.tsx`) calls `openChatWithContext(...)` **without** a `weekTheme`; `openChatWithContext` then wrote the thread's nested `context` object as `{ source, itemTitle, weekTheme }`, so `weekTheme: undefined` (and `itemTitle: undefined` for callers that omit it) landed in the `addDoc` and plain Firestore (`getFirestore(app)`, no `ignoreUndefinedProperties`) rejected the whole write. **Fix:** build the nested `context` so absent fields are **omitted, not written** (`source` always; `...(context.itemTitle ? { itemTitle } : {})`; `...(context.weekTheme ? { weekTheme } : {})`). Top-level thread fields are safe (`title`/`lastMessagePreview` already fall back to `initialMessage`; `chatContext` required; message `addDoc.content` always present). Superset spread — defined fields still written exactly as before, so other `openChatWithContext` callers are unchanged. **Behavior-verified:** with no week theme set, **Find a video** on an academic plan item opens Shelly's chat on a new thread seeded with the `"Find a short, kid-friendly video to help teach: …"` question, no Firestore error, seeded message present. No `ignoreUndefinedProperties` flip (out of scope — 3rd undefined-field bug, separate owner decision). Branch `claude/wizardly-brown-tfk5eg`. | `src/features/shelly-chat/openChatWithContext.ts` |

| **DATA-10** | 2 | **FIXED** | **Enable `ignoreUndefinedProperties` on client Firestore init — retires the undefined-write rejection class app-wide (writes omit undefined fields instead of throwing).** We hit this bug class 4× recently (FUNC-10 `chapterTitle`, FUNC-11 `weekTheme`/`itemTitle`, the latent video-logger `subjectBucket`), each needing its own conditional-spread guard. **Root cause of the class:** the single client Firestore init was plain `getFirestore(app)`, so any `setDoc`/`addDoc` carrying an `undefined`-valued field threw `FirebaseError [invalid-argument]` and rejected the whole write. **Fix (one line):** `src/core/firebase/firestore.ts` now inits via `initializeFirestore(app, { ignoreUndefinedProperties: true })` (confirmed the **single** client init — `initializeFirestore` is the first Firestore call; nothing else calls `getFirestore` in `src/`). Client writes with `undefined`-valued fields now **silently omit** those fields instead of throwing — the desired outcome for the optional fields all known instances involved. Existing defensive guards (`buildChapterPoolItem` conditional spread, `openChatWithContext`'s, the video logger's `subjectBucket`) **left in place** — redundant now but harmless and self-documenting. **Out of scope (hard):** the `functions/` Admin SDK side — `getFirestore()` is called locally across many task files with no central init and Admin `.settings({...})` can only be set once before first use, so it needs its own careful refactor; every bug instance was client-side. **Verified:** `tsc -b`, build, vitest (2674 ✓), lint clean (0 errors). Run SOLO. | `src/core/firebase/firestore.ts` (one edit: `getFirestore`→`initializeFirestore` import + init) |

| **TEST-05** | 1 | **FIXED (landed on `main` via PR #1621, 2026-07-25)** — this row is the incident record | **`origin/main`'s type check went red, which silently skipped every branch's tests in CI.** `npx tsc -b` failed on a clean checkout of `main` with exactly three errors, all in test files: `src/features/monthly-review/photoRefs.test.ts` (6,32) + (7,35) `TS2353` — two `PhotoRef` fixtures written as `{ url, caption }`, a shape `PhotoRef` has never had (the real type in `src/core/types/monthlyReview.ts` requires `id`/`storagePath`/`source`/`sourceDocId`/`capturedAt`) — and `src/features/quest/questModelSync.test.ts` (9,40) `TS2556` — `const mockDoc = vi.fn(() => ...)` infers a **zero-parameter** call signature, so the `doc: (...args: unknown[]) => mockDoc(...args)` spread three lines below had no rest parameter to land in (`mockGetDoc`/`mockSetDoc` are bare `vi.fn()` and accept anything, which is why only line 9 errored). **The blast radius is the point, and is the reason this row exists:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test` job runs Lint → Type check → Run tests **in that order**, so a failing type check makes Actions skip the "Run tests" step entirely. Every PR in flight showed a red `test` job it did not cause, and **no branch's tests actually executed in CI** for as long as this sat on `main` — a green-looking suite that was not running. CI on `main`'s own tip (`66a987c`) is a recorded `failure`, confirming it was `main`'s breakage and not any branch's. **Why it survived:** both files pass at *runtime*, so a green local `npm test` never surfaces it; only `tsc` sees it. An incremental `tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo` cache can also mask it locally — delete it to reproduce. **How it was fixed:** the repair landed on `main` in **PR #1621** (commit `21002a2`), which carried the same two-file fix as a prerequisite commit so its own branch could go green — reshaping the `photoRefs` fixtures to the real `PhotoRef` type via a `photo(id)` factory, and typing the `questModelSync` mock variadic (`vi.fn((...args: unknown[]) => { void args; … })`). A follow-up worth considering: run the type check and the tests as independent jobs (or `continue-on-error` the ordering) so a type failure can never masquerade as, or suppress, a test result. | `src/features/monthly-review/photoRefs.test.ts`, `src/features/quest/questModelSync.test.ts` (both fixed on `main` via #1621); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (step ordering — the follow-up, not changed) |

Because it is a near- and not a literal collapse, the **required pairwise-inequality test passes on `main` too** — it ships as a regression guard, and the behavioural tests are the fail-pre-fix ones. **Fix 1 (cleanup, local/free/instant — no AI call added):** four pure helpers. (a) **Sample inside the crop, not the photo** — `sampleBorderRgb` gains an optional `region` + `insetFraction` so the ring never starts on the outermost pixels; crop path 4%, "use whole image" 8% (`DEFAULT_`/`WHOLE_IMAGE_BORDER_INSET_FRACTION`). (b) **Sample the paper, not the scene** — `pickBackgroundSample` splits the ring's luminance into two clusters (1-D 2-means, deterministic min/max seeding) and, when separated **and** both hold ≥15% of the ring, prefers the **lighter** cluster, unless the darker one is decisively flatter (rescues dark construction paper on a bright rug); rule stated in a comment. **Why the photo failed:** the old plain median of the whole ring landed *between* paper and carpet — the wrong colour for either, so the paper survived opaque — and the whole ring's std dev tripped the `maxBackgroundStdDev` gate (35) into the weak HSL fallback. Feeding the gate the **chosen cluster's own** std dev is what unblocks it; both halves asserted on the carpet fixture. (c) **Drop the specks** — `removeSmallIslands`, connected-component pass whose bound (`computeMinIslandPixels`) is the **lower** of a frame fraction and a fraction of the largest island, so it tracks the drawing and not the camera's megapixels; **the largest island is always kept** whatever the threshold says (a drawing is legitimately several strokes apart). (d) **Let the graphite live** — `boostInkContrast` pushes surviving ink away from the background luminance, hue preserved by scaling all three channels together. **The regression rail is structural, not a tuning hope:** the gain tapers to exactly 1.0 and **skips pixels already ≥`fullRange` (120) from the background**, so marker — far from the paper by construction — is **byte-identical**, asserted as such. ORIGINAL never modified; every knob overridable via `CleanSketchOptions` with the current values as documented fallbacks (`borderSampleSize` 20 / `tolerance` 60 / `featherMultiplier` 1.5 / `edgeSoftness` 1 / `maxBackgroundStdDev` 35 all unchanged). **Fix 2 (styles):** each look names its own **palette, line weight and shading** via a `VisualRecipe` table; a theme picked **without** an explicit base style now **owns the whole look** rather than inheriting the watercolor sentence (that inheritance is what made the nine options converge), while an explicitly named style keeps both blocks so the book reimagine path (`useBackgroundReimagine`, always names a style) is unchanged in shape; the homogenising tail becomes an explicit do-not-drift instruction. **Option ids and the default are untouched so saved stickers do not re-map**; `fancyStyleLabel` lifted out of `DrawingGroupCard` so the library's version chips + aria-labels read from the same table the picker does. Reproduced with a probe before changing anything; the darker cluster now wins only when the lighter one is *actually busy* (`stdDev > minNoisyStdDev`, default 10) **and** the darker is materially flatter (strict `<`). *P2:* the dust bound scaled with the **camera**, not the drawing — 0.0002 of a 4000×3000 photo is 2,400 px, enough to erase an eye dot, a period or the dot of an "i"; rebuilt as `computeMinIslandPixels` (lower of 0.00002 of frame and 0.0005 of the largest island, resolved after labelling via a callback), an order of magnitude safer and tighter still for a sparse drawing. No vowel teams (boat, rain, seed). The hat is big. Sam can hop."*), which also replaces the by-age sample page inside the OUTPUT JSON schema; and **stated PRECEDENCE** over THEME GUIDANCE's `VOCABULARY STYLE`, over the sight-word slice's planner framing, and over *"Contractions are fine"* (**no contractions at Level ≤4**). The old RULES line becomes a pointer to the block — two statements of one constraint, one vague and one concrete, is how the vague one wins. **`sentenceTargetFor({ phonicsLevel, age })`** replaces `sentenceTargetForAge` at all three call sites: **L1-2 → 1-2 sentences (3-6 words); L3-4 → 2-3 (4-8); L5-6 → 2-3 (6-10); L7-8 → 2-4 (8-14)**, monotone non-decreasing, L1-2 shorter than the old ≤7 row; **age is the fallback only** (`sentenceTargetForAge` is kept and still exported for it). Content **stakes** still follow age, deliberately — a 10-year-old decoding at Level 2 gets real stakes in words he can read. **Finding 1 fixed by REMOVAL, not by precedence alone (the prompt's "pick one, justify it").** `wordMastery` is no longer in `TASK_CONTEXT` for the three story tasks. Justification: a precedence line asks the model to resolve a contradiction we can simply not create, and *"SUGGESTION: Generate or assign a sight word story targeting these struggling words"* is too concrete a directive for any rule to reliably neutralise. Nothing is lost — the only thing that slice contributed to a story was a word list, and it contributed the wrong one; the block prints the right one. `sightWords` **stays** (descriptive, and the source of the safe list), with the precedence line now covering its planner-facing framing. **Part 3, one fix then honesty.** `handleGenerateStory` parses the reply (`sanitizeAndParseJson`, never throws — an unparseable reply flows to the client exactly as today with **no** report and **no** fix, so every FEAT-169 failure path is untouched), checks it, and on a failure spends **exactly ONE** focused revise call: `buildStoryReadabilityFixPrompt` carries the story JSON, the per-page hard-word list and the same READING LEVEL block — **no beats, no theme, no family context**, each of which is a reason to drift. The fix is adopted only if it **parsed**, kept the **same page count**, and has **strictly fewer** hard words (`shouldKeepFixedStory`, pure); a tie or a throw keeps the original, so a bad fix can never cost the parent the story they already have. **Never a loop.** The response gains `readability { phonicsLevel, levelSource, passed, hardWords[], revised }` next to `stopReason`; `stopReason` deliberately stays the GENERATION's. Both calls are billed to `aiUsage`; the log line carries `readabilityLevel=N readability=pass\|fail hard=N revised=yes\|no`. Cost ceiling: **at most one extra call per generation**, at the same `maxTokensForPageCount` budget. **Part 4, the honest line.** `storyDraftMessage` gains `storyReadabilityClause`: *"— 2 words may be above London's level: castle, ready."*, plus *"(estimated from age — set London's phonics level under Working Levels on the Skill Snapshot for a better fit)"* when `levelSource === 'age'`. De-duped, capped at 6 named words then counted, singular/plural correct, appended as a new sentence when the line already closed one and as an em-dash clause when it did not — so **every pre-FEAT-176 line is byte-identical**. Plain and blameless (it reports on the STORY, never on the child), no error styling, **no new UI**: the parent fixes it in the revise chat they already have. *Rails held:* the pure module has no I/O and is **not** moved to `shared/` (the client only reads the returned `readability` field); no change to page count, the token budget, FEAT-169's three failure messages, the style/theme image path (FEAT-169/172/173/174) or the sight-word channel (`resolveStoryWords` untouched, typed words still win); read-only on `sightWordProgress` / `wordProgress` / `skillSnapshots` and **nothing writes a level** (`resolveStoryReadingLevel` gained one additive `phonics: number \| null` field instead of re-parsing its text); not name-gated (nothing reads `isLincoln` or a child's name); nothing near hours / XP / diamonds / compliance / `firestore.rules` / the art quota. Ran alongside FEAT-175 with **zero file overlap** (checked). *Tests:* **+82 assertions across 3 new files** (`storyDecodability.test.ts` 33, `storyReadingLevelBlock.test.ts` 22, `tasks/__tests__/generateStory.readability.test.ts` 17) plus 10 client assertions in `storyPracticeWords.test.ts`. **21 fail pre-fix**, verified by reverting the BEHAVIOUR while keeping every module and export present (so the reds are behavioural, not compile errors): all 13 handler cases, the 3 `TASK_CONTEXT` `wordMastery` cases, the 3 "the block reaches all three story prompts" wiring cases, and the 2 `storyDraftMessage` clause cases. The remaining new assertions — the classifier table, the tolerance table, the block's own content, `sentenceTargetFor`, `storyReadabilityClause` — pass in that experiment because their functions exist in it; on true `origin/main` they fail by absence. 4 pre-existing tests were **updated, not deleted** (2 FEAT-173 prompt-line strings that named the removed WORD MASTERY slice, 1 `resolveStoryReadingLevel` deep-equal for the additive `phonics` field, 3 `TASK_CONTEXT` rows) — no test was weakened. *Verified:* root **446 files / 6666 tests, all green** (Step 0 baseline on this `origin/main`: 443 / 6584 → **+3 files / +82 tests**); functions **50 files / 1204 tests** green (baseline 47 / 1132); `npx tsc -b --force` clean; lint **0 errors** (the 3 pre-existing `sessionTimer` warnings, unchanged from baseline); `docs:check` **HARD PASS**; the fix prompt gets the complete story; the return is re-serialized from the new pure `mergeFixedStory` (fixed fields win, only absent keys restored, `pages` never restored) so a model that quietly omits a field cannot reach the client. **P2: a denser fix could win on a technicality.** `shouldKeepFixedStory` compared only `totalHardWords` (the sum of per-page DISTINCT counts), so trading three distinct above-level words for one repeated a dozen times scored "better" while reading worse. It now compares the outcome whole: a fix that PASSES the tolerance is kept outright; otherwise it must improve the distinct count AND worsen neither the occurrence ratio nor the worst page. **P2: the honest line under-reported.** `hardWords` is capped at 12 and the client counted that array, so a story with 30 words above the level announced "12" — the one thing an honesty feature must not do. The response now carries an untruncated `hardWordCount` (`distinctHardWords.length`); the clause reports it and NAMES only the sample, floored at the number actually named so it can never report fewer than it lists, and optional client-side so an older deploy falls back to the sample length. *Round tests:* **9 new assertions, 5 fail pre-fix** (verified by reverting each fix while keeping every module present). **One earlier assertion was TIGHTENED, not added:** the "what the fix prompt carries" test used a bare `toContain("missedWords")` that matched the prompt's own instruction text rather than the story JSON, so it passed against the broken code — it now slices to the JSON and asserts `"missedWords":["pretty"]`. Codex flagged `PROMPT_FIX`; the same shape was in **all four**, so all four were swept: each existing summary instruction now points at **End of run** and keeps its own content contract *under* the `CODEX ROUND:` first line, rather than a second summary being added beside it. **One more thing the round itself taught, folded in:** the fix push drew **no** second review, because Codex reviews on PR open, on a draft going ready, and on an `@codex review` comment — **not** on every push (its own about-box says so, and this PR's second 10-minute window confirmed it: zero new reviews on the fix commit). So finding 2's window would have timed out silently on every run; the protocol now says to **ask** for the follow-up round before polling it. **The requested round then raised a fourth finding (P1), which the run was standing in at the time:** the numbered flow ran poll → fix → ask → poll → summary *once*, so a finding on the follow-up round had no path back — a run could stop on an unanswered review or call it `safe to merge`. The control is `!applied`-gated — post-Apply the cards are a mirror with no Apply bar, and changing a live day is Today's job — and parent-gated at the write as well as the UI (`/planner/chat` sits outside `RequireParent`). A set-aside day shows no budget chip and no *"No items"* — both true sentences and both wrong, reading as a plan that failed to fill rather than one that was declined. The full rule is in `CLAUDE.md`; every template carries a one-sentence version **in its body, before End of run**, because it governs the work rather than the review, and `PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md` — whose whole deliverable is counts — carries it directly under its opening paragraph. **(3) Poll to a result, not to the clock.** Ten minutes is a **ceiling, not a duration**: poll every 30 seconds, act on the first qualifying signal, and a window that has already produced its answer is over. This is the half that actually costs the owner his afternoon — Codex answered #1810 in roughly seven minutes and #1811 faster, so three windows slept out at ten minutes is thirty minutes of pure waiting for answers already in hand. The summary now also **reports the timings** (a line after the `CODEX ROUND:` line, e.g. *"rounds: 6m, 4m, clean at 3m"*). **(4) The cap follows the size of the diff.** The flat *"at most three rounds"* is replaced by: measure at open with `git diff --shortstat origin/main...HEAD` and state the figure in the PR body so the cap is auditable; **changed lines** = insertions + deletions as `--shortstat` reports them, **under 500 → at most two rounds, 500 or more → at most three** — an exact boundary, so two runs cannot classify the same PR differently. Behaviour at the cap is unchanged — address what you can, post `CODEX ROUND: open — do not merge yet` naming exactly what is outstanding and on which head, and stop; the human decides whether to merge, open a follow-up, or paste the remainder into a new run. Because (1) ends the run on a clean round, **the cap only ever binds on a PR still raising findings** — and a small diff still raising real findings at its cap is a diff that should have been two runs. Both data points fit: #1811 converged at round 3 on a large diff; #1810 was a docs PR that never converged. **The ten-minute ceiling was left alone on purpose.** There is no evidence yet that it is wrong — only that runs *sleep through* it — and lowering a timeout and stopping the sleeping are two different changes; change (3) makes runs stop sleeping and change (3)'s reporting line starts collecting the per-round timings a future tuning would need. Revisit once several runs have reported them. **Codex round 1 raised two P2s and both were right.** The first turned the new rule on this very row: DOC-23's own figures — *2/2/0*, *4/4/5*, *twelve of thirteen* — are hand-counted from two PRs' review histories, with no committed derivation, which is precisely what the rule forbids. It could not be fixed by writing one: the source of truth is GitHub, not the tree, and this run is **docs-only** by rail, so a script was not an option either. The honest answer was to **scope the rule and then obey it** — in-repo counts must be derived; out-of-repo figures are cited by PR number and round commit SHA and marked hand-counted — and to apply that to DOC-23's own numbers, including a parenthetical in `CLAUDE.md` saying its two headline figures are hand-counted from PR #1810 and that this run's round 1 raised exactly that. A rule that cannot be satisfied for any number about anything outside the repo would have been quietly ignored by the next run; scoping it is what makes it enforceable. The second P2 was that `~500` is not an executable boundary — two runs could classify the same PR either way, contradicting the stated goal of an auditable cap — so the tilde is gone and the comparison is exact, in every file named above. **Codex round 2 raised one more P2, and it was the same finding one level down.** With the external-source exception in place, the row still asserted *"Four changes"*, *"the five files"*, *"the four templates"* and *"all five files"* — counts whose source of truth **is** this repository, with no committed derivation, so the policy was still violating itself on introduction. **Fixed by naming rather than counting:** the row now lists `CLAUDE.md` and each template by filename, which is its own check — a named list cannot go stale against a recount the way a number can. The rule gained one clause **beyond** what the finding asked, because without it the rule forbids a future run from writing *"6 files changed"* even while pasting `git diff --numstat`, and an unsatisfiable rule is an ignored one (round 1's lesson, one level down): **the case it exists for is a survey** — a count read across a body of code larger than the change, which is expensive to recount and moves when you fix one of its parts — whereas a count over the run's **own diff** is pinned by that diff, so naming the command that prints it is derivation enough, and a short list is better named than counted. **This is the last scoping clause**: two rounds of narrowing a rule under review pressure is the point at which further narrowing would leave mostly exceptions, and the rule now says plainly what it is for. **Codex round 3 came back clean on `798067d9`, and the run closed on it immediately** — which is change (1) being exercised by the change that introduced it. **The rounds took 3m, 3m and clean at 4m** (asked 12:39 / 12:46 / 12:54 UTC, answered 12:42 / 12:49 / 12:58), against a 10-minute ceiling — the first timings recorded under change (3), and already the evidence for its premise: under the old *poll-the-whole-window* reading this run would have spent **30 minutes waiting** for answers that arrived in **10**. ## 7. Triggers (phone-first cheat-sheet)

Everything below is either fully automatic or a single short message pasted into Claude Code web.
No local commands, ever.

### Fully automatic (set once)
- **Monthly audit** — scheduled Claude Code task, same as the /3-day health audit. Task prompt:
  > Read `docs/review/prompts/PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md` and execute it fully.

  Suggested schedule: 1st of the month, after the health audit. It auto-applies safe doc fixes and
  opens a PR for everything else. You just review + merge from the phone.

### One-line triggers (paste into Claude Code web on the repo)
- **Run a fix** (you pick the issue ID from §6):
  > Read `docs/review/prompts/PROMPT_FIX.md` and run it for ISSUE_ID: DATA-01

- **Run the audit now** (off-schedule, e.g. before a design session):
  > Read `docs/review/prompts/PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md` and execute it fully.

- **Just triage / ask** (in the Claude.ai home-base chat, not Claude Code):
  > Read REVIEW_HOME_BASE.md and the latest audit report. What should I fix next and why?

### What is and isn't automated (by design)
- **Auto, no touch:** the audit, stat/doc corrections, PR creation.
- **One tap from you:** merging any PR.
- **Deliberately manual:** fixes that change real code or data — compliance hours, XP ledger, charter
  preamble. These propose-and-stop so a human decides. That's a safety feature for a system holding a
  child's school records, not a gap to close.



## 8. Conventions for this system

- **Design here, build there.** This home base produces decisions and prompts. Claude Code makes the code changes, always on a branch, always reviewed before merge.
- **Inspect → validate → propose for anything touching an invariant.** Hours math, XP ledger, and the additive-hours rule are never auto-fixed. They land as a proposal in the ledger for a human call.
- **One issue ID per fix run.** Keeps PRs small and reviewable.
- **Ledger is the memory.** If it isn't in the ledger, it didn't happen. Every audit and fix updates it.
- **A ledger row is five cells, and §6 is ONE table — `[ledger-shape]` in `docs:check` is HARD on both (2026-09-09).**
  Two ways a row breaks, both of which leave the file parsing fine and every ID, status and anchor intact, so nothing
  else here catches them — and both of which had made most of the ledger unreadable on a phone for months:
  **(1)** an unescaped `` `|` `` inside a code span is still a cell separator, so a row writing a union type like
  `` `status:'new'|'making'` `` spills into phantom columns — **write `\|` inside backticks** (34 rows were affected,
  one as far as 13 cells); **(2)** a **blank line inside the table ends it**, and the rows after it have no header to
  belong to, so they render as raw text with the pipes and asterisks showing (six stray blanks had split §6 into eight
  fragments: 463 rows, of which 100 rendered as a table and 363 as literal markdown). The two are checked together
  because a cell count is only meaningful once the table's extent is known, and (2) is what decides that extent.
  Short rows fail too, so a row with its evidence merged into the Title cell needs an explicit empty `|` at the end.
- **Environment is Claude Code web, phone-first.** Nathan rarely runs anything locally. Claude Code web executes all builds/lint/tests/git in its own environment as part of running a prompt. No prompt should ask the human to run a command, install tooling, or use a local shell. The human's actions are limited to: pasting a prompt, uploading files, and reviewing/merging PRs from the phone.
- **A run ends when the Codex round is answered — then it stops (DOC-18).** After opening the PR a run polls the
  automated review for up to 10 minutes — the **inline review threads**, not just the PR's comments, which is where
  Codex puts its findings — fixes what it raises in the same PR, polls another full window against the new head
  commit, and posts its **one** summary whose **first line** is `CODEX ROUND: done — safe to merge` / `… none arrived
  in 10 min — safe to merge` / `… open — do not merge yet`.
  At most three rounds. If a third round still raises findings, address what you can, post `CODEX ROUND: open — do not merge yet` naming exactly what is outstanding and on which head, and stop. The human decides whether to merge, open a follow-up, or paste the remainder into a new run.
  It then stops: no PR subscription, no check-in, reminder or scheduled task, no staying resident to watch CI.
  Merge only a PR whose first summary line says `safe to merge`; a fix needed after that goes on a new branch and PR.
  Full protocol: `CLAUDE.md` › AI Development Operating Model › **End of run**.
